title: Oracle SOA Integration for C2M (Web Services & APIs)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Oracle Utilities C2M + WebLogic 14c administration; middleware/database/integration work, production-impact care).

Oracle Utilities C2M/CC&B/MDM + WebLogic 14c authored from Oracle's official product + OUAF docs; version-specific details (C2M 25.4/min v2.9, WebLogic 14c) cited or flagged 'verify for your version'; My-Oracle-Support-gated patches/notes are pointed to, not reproduced. Automation is WLST (Jython)/shell/SQL, not PowerShell.
hook: Integrate C2M with the enterprise via SOA, web services, and APIs
problem: C2M rarely stands alone — it exchanges data with meters, billing, analytics, and enterprise systems, often through Oracle SOA and web services/APIs. This solution defines the SOA integration approach for C2M: composites and adapters between C2M and other systems, inbound/outbound web services (IWS), and API patterns — so integrations are consistent, supportable, and observable, pilot-first.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the C2M integration model: Oracle SOA composites/adapters, IWS inbound/outbound web services, and API patterns.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (SOA Suite where used, C2M IWS, endpoints/credentials, pilot).
Implementation Guide — exact steps to design and deploy the named SOA composites/adapters and IWS, apply consistent authN/error-handling/observability, and validate the integrations, pilot-first.

5 automation scripts (WLST/Jython, shell & SQL) — environment/config discovery, per-node validation, a health/coverage report, safe remediation (dry-run by default), and a scope/target helper — authentic to C2M & WebLogic administration.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (integration flows, errors handled, observable) plus Best Practices for supportable, low-lock-in integration.
short: Define the SOA integration approach for C2M — composites/adapters, inbound/outbound IWS, and API patterns — so integrations are consistent, supportable, and observable, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
